romanized_malayalam_availability.notes: Publicly available Romanized Malayalam corpora for customer-support domain were not located during this assessment. Romanized Malayalam is uncommon in large public corpora; research groups have ad-hoc Romanized datasets but provenance and licensing vary.

code_mixed_malayalam_english.notes: Code-mixed Malayalam-English corpora exist in some research papers but curated, license-clean, complaint-domain code-mixed datasets were not found. Collection/annotation would be required.

recommended_option.description: Collect a genuine native-Malayalam, domain-targeted (UPI/banking/customer-support) dataset with human annotation for intents. This provides the strongest scientific validity.
recommended_option.rationale: Domain alignment, label validity, provenance, and annotation quality are critical for intent classification. Existing public corpora are general-domain or parallel/translation-focused and do not reliably provide complaint-level intents.

pragmatic_interim.description: Create a small human-annotated Malayalam evaluation/test set while collecting larger native data. Use FLORES/Samanantar/OSCAR/mC4 only for tokenizer/language-resource experiments, not for intent labels.
pragmatic_interim.rationale: Enables initial experiments and comparisons without altering validated training data or fabricating labels.

tokenization_notes: Large general-domain Malayalam corpora (OSCAR, mC4, IndicNLP) provide sufficient data for tokenization/subword experiments; however, domain mismatch limits conclusions about tokenizer performance for UPI complaint intents. Romanized Malayalam tokenization requires genuine Romanized data; otherwise, experiments risk being non-representative.
limitations_and_risks: No public Malayalam customer-support or banking-specific intent dataset was located. Using general-domain corpora risks domain mismatch. Translating existing English/NON-Malayalam complaint data into Malayalam without human verification creates semantic drift and invalidates intent labels.
next_steps: Plan a targeted data collection protocol for native Malayalam UPI/banking customer complaints (privacy-safe, consent-aware), including annotation guidelines matching Step 3C's strict UPI labels.
Create a small human-annotated Malayalam test set (50–500 examples) drawn from customer forums, support logs (with permissions), or curated examples, and keep it separate from training data.
Use IndicNLP/OSCAR/mC4 and FLORES/Samanantar resources for tokenizer and cross-lingual alignment preparatory work only after licensing checks.
